When I was 22, I moved to New York to work at an investment bank. It was the thing to do, the sign that you "made it."

I couldn't imagine doing it today:
- Pay $4,400 a month for a 383 sq ft walk-up
- Make six figures and live paycheck to paycheck
- Spend $500 on a Hinge date (her fifth this week) and still get ghosted
- Take a white-collar job that AI will replace right when you start making real money
- Leave your watch at home when you take the subway
- Commute in to sit on Teams calls with bosses who work remotely

Today I'd take a job in Dallas, get a Porsche, buy a house at 26, and fly to New York or Miami when I get bored.
